Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 101, verse 1:

﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ (al-Qari'ah): the Resurrection, which strikes the hearts with its terrors.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 101, verse 2:

﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ This is to magnify its matter (تهويل لشأنها). The two words ﴿ما﴾ (mā) and ﴿القارعة﴾ (al-Qāriʿa) are a mubtada' (subject) and a khabar (predicate), and the khabar is ﴿القارعة﴾ (al-Qāriʿa).

﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ "Made you know" (أعلمك). "What the Striking Calamity is" (ما القارعة) adds emphasis to its awe-inspiring nature (زيادة تهويل لها).

The first ما (in ما القارعة) is the mubtada' (the grammatical subject), and what follows it is its khabar (the predicate). The second ما, with its predicate, is in the position of the second object of أدرى (adrā, "to make know").

﴿On the Day﴾: its governing word (al-nasib, the word that determines its grammatical case, i'rab) is indicated by "the Striking" (al-qari'a), meaning it strikes. ﴿People will be like scattered moths﴾, like the swarming locusts that spread out, some surging into others in bewilderment until they are summoned to the reckoning.
And the mountains will be like wool carded out (al-ʿihn al-manfush), like fluffed-out wool (al-ṣūf al-mandūf), in the lightness of their movement, until they level with the earth.

Translation:

﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾ — meaning, whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 101, verse 7:

﴿So he will be in a pleasant life﴾ in Paradise, meaning one characterized by contentment (riḍan), in that he is content with it, i.e., it is pleasing to him (marḍiyyah lahu).
﴿But as for him whose scales are light﴾, meaning, whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.
﴿Then his mother﴾, that is, his dwelling-place, ﴿is an abyss﴾.
﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ i.e., what is *al-Hawiyah* (the Bottomless Pit)?

﴿Nārun ḥāmiyah﴾ (a blazing fire): it is intensely hot. The hāʾ in hiyah is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ as-sakt), which is retained both in connected speech and at pause; and in one reading it is dropped in connected speech.
